policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the phrase as the temporal clause "in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt", which both readings support equally. The qere הוֹצִיאִ֥י is the hiphil infinitive construct with a 1cs suffix ("my bringing them out"); the ketiv הוציא is the same infinitive written without the suffix vowel-letter, and the first-person subject the ASV supplies is already fixed by the speaker of the surrounding oracle ("I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them"). No italicized supply and no ASV textual note is attached to the phrase, so the difference is orthographic and invisible in English. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
